The toy author's reference

PCEStudio runs Lua toys on emulated PC Engine hardware. This page is generated from the runtime's own tables, so every range, cap and refusal code below is the one the code enforces.

The toy Registers Palettes and colour Sprites and the SAT Raster: changes per line Pads The timer Passwords Sound: the PSG Budgets and limits Refusal codes

The toy

A toy is one Lua file. It draws to a 256x224 picture on the PC Engine's VDC and VCE through a small set of calls; everything it does is checked against the hardware's own limits before it is stored.

Three entry points, all optional:

functionwhen it runs
init()once, after the file's top-level statements
frame(t, f)every video frame; t = f/60 seconds, f = frame number
raster(line)every VDW display line 0..223 of the frame, after frame(), for per-line changes

State is ordinary Lua globals and persists across frames. A frame is deterministic: t is f/60, not the clock.

function frame(t, f)
  reg("BXR", floor(t * 32))
end

function raster(line)
  pal(0, line % 512)
end

Registers

A toy may set three VDC registers with reg(name, value). The value must be a whole number in the register's range; anything else is reg-range. Any other name is reg-forbidden — the toy host writes only these, and the rest of the VDC belongs to the ROM.

registerrangewidthwhat it doesmanual
BXR0..102310-bitbackground horizontal scroll, in pixels (VDC R07)VDC H7-7
BYR0..5119-bitbackground vertical scroll, in lines (VDC R08)VDC H7-7
CR0..2558-bitcontrol: BB background on (bit 7), SB sprites on (bit 6), and the VDC interrupt enables (RC bit 2 is the line interrupt)VDC H7-5
function frame(t, f)
  reg("BXR", 64 + floor(32 * sin(t)))
  reg("BYR", 0)
  reg("CR", 0x80 | 0x40)
end

The VDC's other registers — the memory and increment controls, the interrupt mask, the line-match register — are not a toy's to write: the ROM configures them and a toy that changes them would break the frame flow both runtimes share.

Palettes and colour

The VCE holds 512 colour entries (CRAM). pal(addr, word) writes one: the address is 0..511 and the word is a 9-bit colour, 0..511. Either one out of range is pal-range.

A colour word is three 3-bit channels: green in bits 6-8, red in bits 3-5, blue in bits 0-2. rgb(r, g, b) builds one, masking each channel to 0..7.

entrieswhat it is
0..25516 background palettes of 16 colours; a BAT cell names one of the 16 in its palette bits
256..51116 sprite palettes of 16 colours; a SAT entry names one of the 16 in its attribute word

Colour 0 of every background palette is the shared backdrop (CRAM $000): a pixel whose colour number is 0 shows CRAM[0] whatever palette its cell named. Sprite pixel 0 is transparent instead, so a sprite palette's entry 0 never shows on a sprite.

function init()
  for i = 0, 15 do pal(i, rgb(0, i * 2, 7 - i)) end
end

Sprites and the SAT

The sprite attribute table holds 64 entries of 4 words each, at VRAM $7F00. sprite(i, spec) fills entry i from a table; sat(i, k, v) writes one raw word. An entry index outside 0..63 is sat-range (sprite-range for the composed form), and so is a field outside its width.

wordfield
0Y; $40 is display row 0
1X; $20 is display column 0
2pattern code, written << 1
3palette | SPBG<<7 | CGX<<8 | HFLIP<<11 | CGY<<12 | VFLIP<<15
sprite fieldrange
x0..1023
y0..1023
pattern0..1023
palette0..15
cgy0..3
spbg, cgx, hflip, vfliptrue or false

CGX doubles the width and CGY picks the height; the six sizes the VDC draws are below. cells is the 64-word VRAM span the pattern occupies.

sizecellsflagsalignment
16x161 cellCGX 0, CGY 01-cell
32x162 cellsCGX 1, CGY 02-cell
16x324 cellsCGX 0, CGY 14-cell
32x324 cellsCGX 1, CGY 14-cell
16x648 cellsCGX 0, CGY 28-cell
32x648 cellsCGX 1, CGY 28-cell

Per display line the VDC collects at most 16 strips of 16 pixels (256 pixels) in SAT order; a 32-pixel sprite asks for two strips. Sprites past the limit are dropped, not refused — that is the line budget, and the editor reports it per line.

function init()
  sprite(0, { x = 32, y = 64, pattern = 0, palette = 1 })
  sprite(1, { x = 80, y = 64, pattern = 0, palette = 2, hflip = true })
end

Raster: changes per line

The PC Engine has no HDMA. The per-line trigger is the VDC's line interrupt (RCR): the ROM arms RCR for line 0x40 + the display line, and the handler runs once for each of the 224 display lines. A toy expresses per-line changes two ways.

1. A callback: define raster(line). Both runtimes call it for every line 0..223 after frame() and record the register and palette writes it makes as that line's entry.

2. A table entry: call raster(line, spec) from frame() (or init() for a static table). spec may set bxr, byr, cr and cram = {{addr, word}, ...}.

what can change per linerangerefusal
bxr0..1023reg-range
byr0..511reg-range
cr0..255reg-range
a colour entry (addr, word)0..511 / 0..511pal-range

A line gets one entry, because the interrupt fires once per line: a second registration for the same line is raster-line-full, and so is more than 64 colour writes in one line's callback. A line outside 0..223 is raster-line.

The VCE keeps CRAM across frames, so a row above this frame's first write still shows the previous frame's value; the runtime carries that in cramPrev. Inside a table entry, registers the entry does not name keep the frame-wide value.

function frame(t, f)
  for line = 0, 223 do
    raster(line, { bxr = line * 2,
                   cram = { { 0, line % 512 } } })
  end
end

Pads

pad[n] is controller n, 1..5. A pad is 2-button: the D-pad, I, II, Select and Run — 8 read-only booleans, refreshed before frame(). Five pads is the multitap; pad 1 is the console's own port.

fieldthe button
pad[n].upUp
pad[n].downDown
pad[n].leftLeft
pad[n].rightRight
pad[n].iI
pad[n].iiII
pad[n].selectSelect
pad[n].runRun

A pad is true while its button is held, not only on the frame it goes down; remember the previous frame when an action should happen once. Writing a pad field is refused (il-pad-write in the IL; the Lua table is read-only).

local was_ii = false

function frame(t, f)
  if pad[1].ii and not was_ii then print("jump") end
  was_ii = pad[1].ii
end

The timer

The HuC6280's 7-bit interval timer is the console's only sub-frame clock (H8-20..H8-22). timer(period, fn) writes the reload register ($1FEC00) and starts it ($1FEC01 bit 0); the downcounter borrows every period+1 ticks of 6,991.3 Hz, sets TIQ and reloads, and fn is called once per interrupt. A period of 0..127 is 128 ticks at most — 143 us to 18.3 ms (H8-21).

The browser host has no sub-frame clock. It accumulates whole timer ticks across frames at 6991.3 Hz and calls fn at the frame boundary, the number of interrupts that happened since the previous frame() — about 116.5 ticks per frame at 60 Hz. The console runs the same count from the real TMA timer, raised as its own interrupt (vector $FFFA), so timerirqs() reports the hardware's figure there.

callwhat it doesrange / refusal
timer(period, fn)starts the TMA timer: the downcounter reloads from period, counts down once per 1024 CPU clocks (6,991.3 Hz) and, on the borrow that sets TIQ, calls fn once and reloads; a period of 0 counts as 1 tick and 127 as 128 (H8-20..H8-22, pcetech §2.2)period 0..127; fn is called once per interrupt, at the frame boundary, (frames elapsed × 116.5) / (period+1) times
timerstop()stops the timer (its Start/Stop flag, $0C01 bit 0, goes to 0)none
timerirqs()the number of timer interrupts since the previous frame() — the figure a capture's per-frame measurement readsnone
local ticks = 0

-- the interrupt: 17 ticks per period = 6,991.3 / 18 = 388 Hz
timer(17, function () ticks = ticks + 1 end)

function frame(t, f)
  -- timerirqs() is what happened during the frame just ended
  pal(0, rgb(ticks & 7, 0, 0))
end

Passwords

A bare HuCard has no save memory, so a toy saves with a password (Dennis, 2026-10-28). password.pack(value) turns a value into a short code starting P1 (base32 alphabet, then a check byte) and password.unpack(code) returns it; a mistyped or foreign code is password-code.

A value is nil, a boolean, an integer, a string, or a table with number or string keys. Every cap is a maximum the round trip holds to; one past it is refused naming the edge, never truncated.

valuemaximumpast it
an integer-1073741824..1073741823password-value
a non-integer numbernone — not an integerpassword-value
a string64 bytespassword-value
a table32 entries, nested 6 tables deeppassword-value
the value's bytes96, before the check bytepassword-value
the whole code200 characterspassword-code

The integer cap is 2^30, not the VM's full 32-bit range: an integer is 32 bits and the zig-zag encoding spends one bit on the sign, so a magnitude of 2^30 doubles to 2^31 and would wrap (card #73).

function frame(t, f)
  local code = password.pack({ high = 1200, level = 3 })
  print(code)
end

Sound: the PSG

The HuC6280 PSG has 6 channels, each a 32-step waveform of 5-bit samples (0..31), plus noise on channels 4 and 5 and an LFO. The model is renderer/pce-psg.js, a literal transcription of Mednafen's pipeline at 44100 Hz.

A toy reaches it three ways. music(index) plays a song the runtime was given — a module read by the tracker route (renderer/pce-dmf.js, renderer/pce-song.js), whose writes are the ones HuTrack's engine makes, one VBlank per frame. sfx(channel, freq, volume, frames) takes a channel from the music the way HuTrack reserves one, loads a 32-step square, sets F and AL, and gives the channel back after frames frames. release(channel) gives a channel back now.

A release does not resume the middle of a held note: the music waits for the next note row on that channel, and that fresh note reloads the instrument's waveform (all 32 steps) even when it has not changed — HuTrack's channel hand-off. The writes go to renderer/pce-psg.js in the frame's order, so a toy's sound is the model's own PCM.

callwhat it doeslimits and refusal
music(index)plays song index from the start — the whole engine restarts, as HuTrack's playSong doesan index into the songs the runtime was given (0..songs-1)
sfx(channel, freq, volume, frames)takes the channel (HuTrack's reserve), loads a 32-step square, sets F = freq and AL = volume, and gives it back after frameschannel 0..5, freq 0..4095, volume 0..31, frames 1..600
release(channel)gives a channel back now (HuTrack's release): control and noise off, and the music waits for a fresh note on itchannel 0..5; a channel no SFX owns is left alone
registernamewhat a write doesmanual
R0channel selectselects the channel R1-R7 act on (0-5); a select alone makes no soundPSG PB-2
R1main amplitudeL/R master volume, one nibble per sidePSG PB-3
R2frequency LSBlow 8 bits of the 12-bit frequency divider FPSG PB-3
R3frequency MSBhigh 4 bits of FPSG PB-3
R4channel controlchannel on/off, DDA mode, and the channel levelPSG PB-3
R5channel balanceper-channel L/R volume, one nibble per sidePSG PB-4
R6waveform dataone 5-bit sample of the 32-step wave; in DDA mode, the held levelPSG PB-4
R7noise controlnoise enable and frequency for channels 4 and 5 onlyPSG PB-6
R8LFO frequency8-bit LFO ratePSG PB-6
R9LFO controlLFO trigger (bit 7) and depth/controlPSG PB-6

F is the PSG's 12-bit divider, so a note's F is 7,159,090 / (64 f). note(name or MIDI) returns it — a name in Lua, a MIDI number in both runtimes (the IL carries no strings).

function init()
  music(0)                        -- the song the page was given
end

function frame(t, f)
  if pad[1].ii then sfx(3, note(76), 24, 10) end
end

Refusal codes

A refusal is a named failure, not a silent drop: the call throws (or the page shows) an error whose code is one of these, and both runtimes use the same code for the same fault.

The toy host (both runtimes) renderer/pce-toyhost.js

raster-line-fulla second raster entry on one line, or too many colour writes on it
reg-forbiddena register a toy may not touch
reg-rangea register value outside the VDC register's width
sat-rangea SAT entry outside 0..63 or a SAT word past $FFFF

sprite-rangea sprite field outside the SAT's range

vram-rangea VRAM word address outside 0..32767 or a word past $FFFF
